summary: Garcin de Tassy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lycée Thiers and under Jean-Daniel Kieffer. He served as Professor of Hindustani at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales and École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1828–1878).

Gareth Fisher is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia in 2006 and served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

Gareth Sparham is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and earned a PhD from the University of British Columbia under Ashok Aklujkar, later teaching at UBC (attested 1997) and Michigan (1999).

Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty appointments at Harvard University (attested 1999), Columbia University (attested 2007), and the University of Chicago (attested 2011).

Gary D. DeAngelis is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who was mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi and William J. Johnson. He served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

Gary Snyder is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley. He held academic posts at the University of California, Davis (~1986–2002) and the University of California, Irvine (attested 2002).

Gary Urton is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He held posts at Colgate University (1978–2002) and Harvard University (2002–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio was an Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf in 1834. He held academic and library appointments at the University of Turin (~1852–1859) and the Royal Library of Turin (~1859–1891).

Gavin D'Costa is a religious studies scholar who was educated at Bedford Modern School and the University of Birmingham (~1980–1985). He was appointed Professor in Catholic Theology at the University of Bristol (~2004).

Gavin Flood is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. His posts include positions at Lampeter, the University of Oxford, the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies, and the University of Stirling.

Gelek is a Tibetologist who served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998). He also held visiting appointments at the University of California and the University of Oxford.

Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under multiple traditional teachers and received formal education at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo.
Gen'ichi Yamazaki was an Indologist and historian who completed his studies at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1963). He served as a professor at Kokugakuin University from ~1976 to 2006.
Genchi Kato was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1896 to 1899 and later served on its faculty from ~1907 to 1934.
Gendun Chophel was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kumbum Monastery, Labrang Monastery, and under Sherab Gyatso. He held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.

Genjun Sasaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who graduated from Kyoto University and studied under multiple teachers. He held posts at Otani University, Harvard University, the University of Hamburg (1956), and Osaka University (attested 1995).
Genryu Kagamishima was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from ~1932 to 1935. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from ~1965 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University (~1949–1956). He held posts at Kokushikan University (~1974–1980) and served as professor emeritus at Rissho University (~1996).
Genzao was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950. He received traditional instruction from Gyang mdzod Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies who studied at Stockholm and Uppsala universities. He held a long-standing post at Uppsala University (~1940–1973) and was later affiliated with Stockholm University (attested 1990).
